Tool-surface ordering must be deterministic across naming, MCP server IDs, and allow/deny lists for a given session/persona/mode/option set (FR-080).
MCP is a transport, not a bypass: tools pass through permission, hook, path, redaction, and event logging policy (K-MCP-1).
Read-only capability lands before write/edit/shell capability; write/edit and bash stay denied until later phases activate them (FR-082).
section9.chirality_mcp_status_dependencies is the runtime validation ID for status/dependency MCP behavior.
In readOnly permission mode, only read-only tools are exposed/allowed; write/edit/bash/network-capable tools are unavailable or hard-denied (FR-091).
Explicit denies from policy, path containment, hook, governance, SDK deny rule, or human gate block tool execution (K-PERM-1).
allowedTools is not a restriction boundary by itself (K-PERM-3).
_STATUS.md is the canonical human-readable lifecycle state source (K-STATUS-1).
Deliverable-local _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv are authoritative for dependencies (K-DEP-1).
mcp__chirality__scaffold is gated; this deliverable covers preview/dry-run behavior, not uncontrolled scaffold writes.

MCP tool definitions and wrapper metadata are unit-tested and deterministic (FR-079).

DEL-06-03 provides the first Chirality-owned in-process MCP read tools so the runtime can expose deterministic project-state operations without opening write, edit, shell, remote MCP, plugin, or domain-operation capability.
DEL-06-03 supports OBJ-005 by keeping tool exposure behind capability policy with explicit hard-deny precedence and MCP wrappers, and OBJ-006 by reading filesystem-native project truth.

Principle: read tools come first; the R2 slice enables SDK read tools and Chirality read MCP tools before write/edit/bash capability. Treat the deliverable as a read-surface and descriptor/wrapper contract.
Principle: MCP is a transport, not a policy escape; in-process Chirality MCP tools must traverse the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event logging policy as SDK built-ins.
Principle: determinism is part of the contract; tool naming, ordering, server IDs, wrapper metadata, and allow/deny behavior should be table-driven or stable for a fixed runtime configuration.

Principle: explicit hard-deny precedence is non-negotiable; allowedTools may auto-approve but is not a restriction boundary, and denies from policy, hooks, path containment, governance, SDK deny rules, or human gates must win.

Principle: filesystem truth remains local and inspectable; status and dependency tools read canonical project files, and unknowns/malformed records produce explicit results rather than inferred project truth.
Keep status_transition and deps_write out of the read-tool slice except as excluded adjacent tools.
Implement only preview/dry-run behavior for mcp__chirality__scaffold unless a later write-surface gate authorizes more.
Prefer a clear Dependencies.csv validation result; behavior when a deliverable has _DEPENDENCIES.md but no Dependencies.csv is TBD and should align with DEL-07-05.
Read _STATUS.md as canonical lifecycle state; do not infer status from folder names, chat state, runtime events, or document presence.
Scope scan should stay bounded to the selected working root and stable deliverable IDs (K-PATH-2).
Permission/start/completion/failure event persistence may depend on R1/R2 runtime plumbing; if unavailable, expose a typed integration seam and tests around expected behavior (FR-083).

PRD-backed details remain usable as warning-qualified direction; closure should not rely on PRD-only wrapper-policy detail until the reference hash is refreshed, a human accepts the current PRD text, or the requirement is corroborated by CONTRACT.md, SPEC.md, TYPES.md, or PLAN.md.
Trade-off: prefer a shared wrapper contract with per-tool metadata and execution handlers over per-tool wrappers, which can drift.
Trade-off: include scaffold dry-run/preview only, with write execution denied or delegated to later gated surfaces.
Trade-off: when Dependencies.csv may be absent early, return an explicit 'not present / not tracked yet' result and do not fabricate dependencies.
Trade-off: keep event emission/adaptation explicit and testable; mark unavailable runtime pieces TBD instead of embedding hidden behavior.
Trade-off: use SDK MCP APIs behind product-owned wrappers and tests; do not leak SDK-shaped public contracts.

Scaffold boundary: allow a deterministic preview of intended scaffold effects, deny or defer filesystem mutation, and move any write-capable scaffold execution to the later governed write/path-hook surface.
mcp__chirality__status_read result shape: parsed _STATUS.md snapshot plus source path, parse warnings, and raw/normalized state fields.
mcp__chirality__deps_read result shape: Dependencies.csv validation summary when present; explicit missing/not-tracked status when absent; warnings sourced to files.
mcp__chirality__scope_scan result shape: bounded package/deliverable scan summary with stable IDs and rejected out-of-root requests.
mcp__chirality__scaffold result shape: preview/dry-run plan showing intended scaffold effects without applying filesystem writes.

The deliverable specifies the initial in-process Chirality MCP read-tool slice for PKG-06, covering deterministic MCP tool descriptors, wrapper metadata, execution behavior, and tests for status read, dependency read, bounded scope scan, and scaffold preview/dry-run.
In scope: preserve read-before-write sequencing by excluding write/edit/bash capability from this deliverable.
Out of scope: general SDK built-in read-tool resolver behavior owned by DEL-06-02.
Out of scope: write/edit path hooks owned by DEL-06-04.
Out of scope: bash governance owned by DEL-06-05.
Out of scope: remote MCP, plugins, and domain-engine operations.
REQ-06-03-001: Chirality-specific deterministic operations in this slice MUST use mcp__chirality__* names.
REQ-06-03-002: the initial read-tool set MUST include mcp__chirality__status_read, mcp__chirality__deps_read, and mcp__chirality__scope_scan.
REQ-06-03-003: the scaffold surface MUST be limited to preview/dry-run behavior and MUST NOT open uncontrolled scaffold writes.
REQ-06-03-004: Chirality-owned tool definitions MUST declare schema, permissions, read-only behavior, concurrency, interruption, execution, and summarization behavior.
REQ-06-03-005: tool-surface construction MUST be deterministic for a given session, persona, mode, option set, SDK version, MCP server set, and permission policy.
REQ-06-03-006: MCP tools MUST pass through the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event logging policy as SDK built-ins.
REQ-06-03-007: denied tools MUST NOT execute and SHOULD be omitted from model context where possible.
REQ-06-03-008: allowedTools MUST NOT be treated as a restriction boundary by itself; restriction MUST rely on deny rules, mode policy, hooks, canUseTool, and/or dontAsk posture.
REQ-06-03-009: in readOnly mode these tools MUST NOT expose or allow write/edit/bash/network-capable actions.
REQ-06-03-010: tool permission/start/completion/failure activity SHOULD be persisted as Chirality runtime events when runtime event plumbing is available.
REQ-06-03-011: status read behavior MUST treat _STATUS.md as the canonical lifecycle state source.
REQ-06-03-012: dependency read behavior MUST treat _DEPENDENCIES.md and Dependencies.csv as dependency truth sources, with Dependencies.csv read/validation where present.
REQ-06-03-013: scope scan behavior MUST be bounded to the workspace/project root contract and must not scan arbitrary external locations.
REQ-06-03-014: unknown or unsupported MCP tool names MUST fail with structured validation errors rather than silent pass-through.

REQ-06-03-015: dependency-read behavior MUST expose explicit structured absence or secondary-summary status when Dependencies.csv is absent and _DEPENDENCIES.md exists, MUST NOT infer rows from prose, and final result schema remains TBD pending DEL-07-05.
